shots.text: Pepsi got paid in submarines. Seventeen of them.
You see, Pepsi had beaten Coke into the Soviet Union, but rubles could not be traded on world markets.
Starting in nineteen seventy-two, Pepsi took Stolichnaya vodka as payment and sold it in America.
It worked. Soviets were soon drinking about a billion servings of Pepsi a year.
But after a boycott over the war in Afghanistan, vodka alone couldn't pay for all that Pepsi.
Then the Soviets offered something they had plenty of: old warships.
In spring nineteen eighty-nine, Pepsi took seventeen submarines, a cruiser, a frigate, and a destroyer.
The submarines were priced at about one hundred fifty thousand dollars each.
You see, Pepsi never wanted a navy. It was only the middleman.
So it sold the whole fleet for scrap.
The next year, Pepsi signed a three billion dollar deal with the Soviets.
Then the Soviet Union collapsed in nineteen ninety-one, and the deal vanished.
